# Bhatti Audit Matrix: manual vs. AI docstrings (UE-6 b)

**Module:** `geodesk.terrain` (arc42 B5.2 contour generator, FR-09), 15 documented symbols.
**Manual version:** `audit/manual_docstring.py`. **AI version:** `audit/ai_docstring.py`, generated by Claude Sonnet from the code with docstrings removed (`audit/undocumented_terrain.py`). The prompt is in the [Use-Verify-Cite log](use_verify_cite_log.md).
**Diff:** `audit/manual_vs_ai.diff` (per-symbol docstring diff, made by `audit/make_docstring_diff.py`).
**Scale:** 1–5 stars per principle (Bhatti et al., *Docs for Developers*, Ch. 5).

## Audit matrix

| Principle | Manual | AI (raw) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Explained**: says why, not only what | ★★★★★ | ★★★☆☆ | Manual links each symbol to FR-09, arc42 B5.x and the W05 API error codes. The AI describes mechanics only and never says why the interval must be ≥ 0.5 m. |
| **Concise**: no filler | ★★★★☆ | ★★☆☆☆ | The AI adds 10 `Args: None` sections, 3 `Raises: None.`, 4 `Returns:` sections on classes, and 5 `Raises` entries for misuse (`FrozenInstanceError` ×3, `IndexError` ×2). The manual version repeats the 7-line Zaisan DEM setup in every example. |
| **Clear**: precise terms | ★★★★☆ | ★★★☆☆ | The AI calls a 2-point segment a "polyline" with "ordered vertices", and calls a float32 file-size estimate "in-memory size". |
| **Usable**: consistent, copy-pasteable examples | ★★★★★ | ★★★☆☆ | Manual: one DEM (`layer_dem_44c1`, origin 650000/5310000) in all 11 examples, as Chinchilla (Ch. 7, pp. 89–90) asks. AI: 6 unrelated grids, 2 origins, including `[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]` at (0, 0). |
| **Trustworthy**: true and verified | ★★★★☆ | ★★★☆☆ | All 15 AI doctests pass and every referenced symbol exists. But the AI misstates `origin` (C1), and that error becomes a 15 m shift in runs 2 and 3. Manual: 2 wrong numbers, caught by doctest before merge (M1). |
| **Average** | **4.6** | **2.8** | |

## Corrections applied to the AI output (≥ 2 required)

| # | Principle | AI text | Problem (how verified) | Correction merged into `src/` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Trustworthy | "The `origin` is the north-west corner of the grid" | Wrong contract: `origin` is the **centre** of the north-west cell. Runs 2 and 3 turned it into `origin=(transform.c, transform.f)`, which moves every contour by (−15 m, +15 m). Proven by `tests/test_geotiff_quickstart.py::test_ai_corner_origin_shifts_contours_by_half_a_cell`. | `origin` docs now say "centre, not outer corner" and give the conversion. A module Quickstart reads a real GeoTIFF; the test runs it. |
| C2 | Clear / Trustworthy | `size_mb`: "Estimated in-memory size of the grid" | The value is rows × cols × 4 bytes, the size of a **float32 GeoTIFF**. A Python tuple of floats takes far more memory. Checked against `_BYTES_PER_CELL = 4`. | Kept the manual wording: "Estimated size of the DEM as a float32 GeoTIFF". |
| C3 | Concise | `Args: None: This is a read-only property.` and 16 similar sections | Pure template filler; napoleon renders it as an empty "Parameters" table. | Removed. Properties use the one-line `type: description` form. |
| C4 | Usable | 6 different example grids (`layer_dem_01`, `[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]`, …) | Readers cannot compare results across classes (Chinchilla Ch. 7, pp. 89–90). | Every example uses the Zaisan DEM `layer_dem_44c1`. |
| C5 | Clear | `ContourLine`: "single contour polyline", "Ordered vertices" | The generator emits one 2-point segment per cell, with no ordering guarantee (see `_cell_segments`). | Kept the manual "One contour segment … order is not guaranteed". Joining segments is not tracked yet (see Sprint 7). |
| C6 | Explained | Classes and `generate()` with no link to requirements | The reader can't tell why limits are 0.5 m, 200 MB and 20 %. | Kept the manual references to FR-09, NFR-01, NFR-05 and the W05 HTTP codes. |

## Where the AI was better (manual corrections adopted from AI)

| # | Manual text | AI text | Why the AI was right | Merged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `nodata`: "or ``None`` if every cell is valid" | "or ``None`` if only NaN values mark missing cells" | `_is_nodata` also treats NaN as missing, so `None` does not mean "every cell is valid". | ✔ |
| A2 | `nodata_ratio()`: no definition of "missing" | "A cell counts as missing if it is NaN or equals the `nodata` sentinel." | Same NaN rule; the manual reader had to read the code. | ✔ |
| A3 | "at least 0.5 m" | "at least :attr:`MIN_INTERVAL_M`" | Links the constant, so the docs can't drift if the limit changes. | ✔ (kept "0.5 m" too) |

## Manual errors found by tests

| # | Where | Error | Caught by |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `ContourGenerator` example | "8 lines" (hand count); the real value is 7 (1 + 3 + 3 per level) | `pytest --doctest-modules` before the merge |
| M2 | `generate()` example | Vertex order of `lines[0]` written the wrong way round | same doctest run |

Both AI and human docstrings needed correction. Only the executable examples caught the numeric mistakes (Bhatti p. 94).
